title: Designing Voice Agents for Real Conversations - Chintan Agrawal & Daniel Wirjo, AWS
talk_summary: AWS solutions architects explain turn-taking in voice agents: VAD, STT-provider endpointing, and a local smart-turn model layered on VAD as a safety net, plus latency budgeting and P95 tail concerns. The core lesson is a cheap fast heuristic gated by a small classifier with a deterministic fallback timer, and preferring P95 over P50 for interactive paths.

takeaways.technique: Fast heuristic + small classifier + deterministic fallback timer
takeaways.what_they_do: Run a cheap local VAD for the basic signal, add a small smart-turn model that only fires when confident, and keep the VAD silence timer as a safety net so the system never waits indefinitely.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If the Smart Turn doesn't fire, your stop second will kick in, like, at the configured latency anyway.
takeaways.numbers: Smart Turn V3.2: 58.9% recall, 68.4% precision, 8MB model; fallback timer ~300ms

takeaways.technique: Optimize P95 tail, not P50, for interactive paths
takeaways.what_they_do: Benchmark models on P95 latency because a single slow response ruins the interaction; they reject models with good P50 but bad tails.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what matters more in voice than maybe anywhere else is that the P95 tail
takeaways.numbers: GPT-4.1 P50 536ms but P95 1.7s; Claude 3 hit over 4s at P95

takeaways.technique: Session reset / context pruning for long multi-turn runs
takeaways.what_they_do: They note instruction-following degrades after 15-20 turns and recommend context pruning or session resets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: after 15 or 20 turn, sometime model starts ignoring parts of the system prompt

takeaways.what_they_do: Classify incoming signals into correction (stop everything), filler (continue quieter), and noise (ignore) instead of stopping on every signal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can start distinguishing between a real interruption and someone just, you know, going um

takeaways.technique: Co-locate components to cut network hops
takeaways.what_they_do: Quindos demonstrated ~500ms voice-to-voice by co-locating all models in the same GPU cluster, eliminating internal network hops.
takeaways.evidence_quote: co-locating all models in the same GPU cluster
takeaways.numbers: ~500ms total vs 1,100-1,300ms standard cloud API setup
